item.title: White House Says "Cannot Tolerate Discrimination Against Coupang" Blue House Responds "Investigation Conducted by Law" (백악관 “쿠팡 차별 용납 못해” 靑 “법대로 조사했다”)
item.description:
White House Says "Cannot Tolerate Discrimination Against Coupang" Blue House Responds "Investigation Conducted by Law" (백악관 “쿠팡 차별 용납 못해” 靑 “법대로 조사했다”)

A U.S. House of Representatives report alleging that the South Korean government is discriminating against Coupang, a company headquartered in the U.S., is showing signs of escalating tensions between South Korea and the U.S. After the White House stated to South Korea that it "will not tolerate unfair practices," the Blue House said on the 3rd that "the content of the report significantly differs from the facts." The Blue House added, "(Coupang) is under investigation and is a kind of suspect," and stated, "We will incorporate our side of the story and resolve this through communication." There are also criticisms that it is problematic that the U.S. government has not been convinced eight months after the Coupang personal information leak incident. <<> The White House said on the 2nd (local time) regarding the U.S. House Judiciary Committee's report on Coupang to this newspaper, "By any reasonable standard, Coupang has been singled out by the Lee Jae-myung administration" and "The Trump administration will not tolerate unfair trade practices, including actions that limit U.S. digital service (companies') access to the Korean market." A White House official also stated that day, "We express deep concern over the South Korean government's discriminatory targeting of U.S. tech companies." <<> On the 1st, the U.S. House Judiciary Committee released a 34-page report titled "Blocking Competition: South Korea's Discriminatory Attacks on a U.S.-Owned Company." The report, primarily based on the testimony of Harold Rogers, the interim representative of Coupang's Korean entity, and documents submitted by Coupang, claimed that "South Korean authorities have targeted Coupang, exposing it to hostile regulations and unfair enforcement." It also included allegations that after a large-scale personal information leak at Coupang in November of last year, a former employee's laptop, suspected of involvement in the leak, was retrieved from China under the direction of the National Intelligence Service (NIS), and that President Lee Jae-myung was aware of the NIS's involvement. <<> After the report became public, South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed regret that it "one-sidedly reflects only Coupang's claims," and the NIS also issued a statement saying the report's content was not factual. Despite these government positions, the White House criticized South Korea for discriminating against Coupang based on the report, calling it an "unfair trade practice." <<> When asked about the White House's stance, Wi Sung-lac, head of the Blue House National Security Office, said on the 3rd that "all investigations into Coupang are being conducted non-discriminatorily in accordance with domestic legal procedures." He added that "the report's claims that the investigation is discriminatory, targeted, or that unfair regulations persist are significantly different from the facts." Director Wi also said, "If a similar information leak had occurred in the U.S., and personal information equivalent to two-thirds of the U.S. population was leaked to China without knowing where it went, it would undoubtedly be a very serious issue in the U.S." <<> Regarding the U.S. House report's claim that the NIS led the process of retrieving the hacking suspect's equipment from China and that the president was aware of it, Director Wi stated, "We had no prior knowledge, nor did we instruct or get involved," and "I first heard about it around mid-December (last year) that a Coupang-related person had retrieved it, calling it 'good news.'" He added that since Coupang's side is one-sidedly reflected in the report, they will communicate while reflecting the government's position. He also said, "We will make efforts to isolate and separate the issue so that it does not affect other issues between South Korea and the U.S." <<> The National Assembly Secretariat also issued a statement that day expressing "regret" over the report. The report claimed about the National Assembly's hearing on Coupang held in December last year that "lawmakers demonstrated a clearly hostile and discriminatory way the South Korean government treats U.S.-based companies," which the secretariat said distorts the facts. The National Assembly Secretariat stated, "Procedures at the hearing, such as swearing in, notifying legal responsibility for false testimony, and adjusting response times, are equally applied to all witnesses," and "interpreting this as a discriminatory measure against a specific company or specific witness is inconsistent with the facts." <<> Since news broke in November last year that the information of 37.56 million people was leaked from Coupang, the South Korean government and National Assembly have taken it seriously and responded. However, in April, about 50 U.S. House Republicans sent an open letter to South Korean Ambassador to the U.S. Kang Kyung-wha demanding "an end to attacks targeting U.S. companies like Coupang," and following the House Judiciary Committee, the White House also expressed concern. <<> It is understood that before the U.S. House Judiciary Committee released its report, the South Korean government explained its position that "the investigation into Coupang is proceeding fairly and according to law without discrimination." However, the report did not include a single line of South Korea's views. Among foreign affairs and security experts, there are concerns that "South Korean diplomatic authorities may not have sufficient influence over the U.S. Congress or the White House." Brody Mullins, a former Wall Street Journal reporter and American investigative journalist, said on social media on the 2nd that "the South Korean government spent $350 million (about 540 billion won) on lobbying and public relations in the U.S. over the past ten years, yet could not prevent criticism from the U.S. Congress and administration." The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated, "The Embassy in the U.S. has hired various advisory firms to efficiently support diplomatic activities toward the U.S. aimed at strengthening the South Korea-U.S. alliance." (한국 정부가 미국에 본사를 둔 쿠팡을 차별하고 있다는 내용의 미 하원 보고서를 두고, 한미 간 공방이 격화될 조짐을 보이고 있다. 미 백악관이 한국을 향해 “불공정 관행을 용납하지 않겠다”고 하자, 청와대는 3일 “보고서 내용이 사실과 크게 다르다”고 했다. 청와대는 “(쿠팡은) 수사 대상이고 일종의 피의자”라며 “우리 이야기도 반영해 소통하며 풀어가겠다”고 했다. 쿠팡 개인정보 유출 사고가 난 지 8개월이 지나도록 미국 정부를 납득시키지 못한 것은 문제라는 지적도 나온다.)

item.title: "New Growth Engine: Aerospace to Be Fostered in Yeongnam" (“새 먹거리 우주항공, 영남서 키울 것”)
item.description:
"New Growth Engine: Aerospace to Be Fostered in Yeongnam" (“새 먹거리 우주항공, 영남서 키울 것”)

President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 3rd at the "National Report Meeting on the Vision for Advanced Industry Development in the Yeongnam Region" held in Jinju, South Gyeongsang Province, "We will establish Yeongnam as a solid leading region for South Korea's advanced industries with overwhelming technological gaps." This is the third national report meeting in Yeongnam, following those in Honam (semiconductor fabs) and Chungcheong (packaging), as part of the follow-up schedule to the "Three Mega Projects for South Korea's Great Leap Forward" announced on the 29th of last month. <<> President Lee said, "Yeongnam is the undisputed No. 1 hub of South Korea's manufacturing industry," adding, "Alongside large-scale investments in next-generation semiconductors and AI data centers, we will intensively foster physical AI sectors, including the nation's largest robot industry innovation belt, automobiles, and the world's top shipbuilding, to reshape manufacturing sites into intelligent industries." He continued, "In particular, aerospace is a new growth engine industry that Yeongnam will cultivate for South Korea," and "The government plans to fully establish a South Coast aerospace industry belt that connects satellites, launch vehicles, future aircraft, and new space industries." President Lee also said, "The central government will promote bold package support combining tax, fiscal, financial, and regulatory measures with infrastructure," adding, "To this end, I, as President, will personally oversee this project closely and stand at the center of its special promotion." <<> At the event, corporate representatives attended and announced specific investment plans for the Yeongnam region. Hanwha Group announced approximately 55 trillion won in the satellite and launch vehicle sectors, Hyundai Motor Group about 42 trillion won in AI-based autonomous driving mobility, Samsung Electronics around 60 trillion won in robots and next-generation battery mass production lines, and SK Telecom 140 trillion won in building AI data center infrastructure exceeding 2 gigawatts (GW). The presidential office reported that LG and Doosan will also announce specific investment plans soon. The total investment scale by these companies, as announced by the government, amounts to at least 312 trillion won. <<> President Lee said at the National Space Committee held at Jinju Gyeongsang National University on the same day, "The government is an expert in speed," and "We will ensure the most efficient and rapid response possible." He added to the committee members, "If you personally think you need to tell me something or it's important, you can send me individual messages directly," urging, "Don't make excuses about lacking communication channels; actively share your opinions." When committee member Kim Soo-jong noted, "To foster a successful aerospace company like SpaceX, it is necessary to significantly ease regulations on rocket launch permit reviews," President Lee responded, "Within the scope that does not threaten public safety, follow-up launch reviews should be relaxed." Along with this, as demands for improving technical regulatory systems arose, he ordered a review of the introduction of a "defense acquisition fast track" to shorten the period for introducing military equipment. (이재명 대통령은 3일 경남 진주에서 열린 ‘영남권 첨단산업 발전비전 국민보고회’에서 “영남을 대한민국의 확고한 첨단산업 초격차 선도 지역으로 세우겠다”고 밝혔다. 지난달 29일 발표한 ‘대한민국 대도약 3대 메가 프로젝트’ 후속 일정으로 호남(반도체 팹), 충청(패키징)에 이어 영남에서 열린 세 번째 국민보고회다.)

item.title: Opposition’s Fast-Track Move to Abolish Prosecution’s Supplementary Investigation Powers… Internal Concerns Grow Over “Significant Side Effects” (與 보완수사권 폐지 속도전에… 내부서도 “부작용 커”)
item.description:
Opposition’s Fast-Track Move to Abolish Prosecution’s Supplementary Investigation Powers… Internal Concerns Grow Over “Significant Side Effects” (與 보완수사권 폐지 속도전에… 내부서도 “부작용 커”)

As the prosecution service is set to be abolished in October and replaced with the Public Prosecution Office and the Major Crimes Investigation Office, the Democratic Party of Korea is accelerating legislative efforts to completely abolish the prosecution’s supplementary investigation powers. However, concerns are emerging not only from the opposition and legal circles but also from within the ruling party that “if the focus remains solely on speed without fully considering the side effects of reforming the criminal justice system, the public could suffer from institutional gaps.” (검찰청이 오는 10월 폐지되고 공소청과 중대범죄수사청(중수청)이 출범하는 가운데, 더불어민주당이 ‘검찰 보완수사권 전면 폐지’ 입법에 속도를 내고 있다. 하지만 야권과 법조계는 물론 여권 일각에서도 “형사사법체계 개편에 따른 부작용을 충분히 고려하지 않은 채 속도전에만 몰두할 경우 국민이 제도 공백에 따른 피해를 볼 수 있다”는 우려가 나오고 있다.)

On the 3rd, Democratic Party acting leader and floor leader Han Byung-do stated during a party meeting, “The amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act, which will be the crowning achievement of prosecution reform, will be carried out with thorough content and swift processing, combining efforts from the floor, policy committee, and legislation and judiciary committee.” The amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act is expected to include the complete abolition of the prosecution’s supplementary investigation powers. In this regard, the Democratic Party formed a task force for the Criminal Procedure Act amendment the previous day and began the formal legislative process. Despite the People Power Party boycotting all parliamentary schedules in protest of the Democratic Party’s unilateral push to elect standing committee chairs, the Democratic Party held the first legislation and judiciary committee meeting of the second half of the 22nd National Assembly without the opposition party. <<> Hardliners within the ruling party argue that the Criminal Procedure Act amendment must be finalized by July. Former Representative Jeong Cheong-rae said, “Let’s finish it before Constitution Day (July 17),” while Representative Kim Yong-min added, “It must be passed by July.” The Rebuilding Korea Party also demanded the previous day, “Let’s complete the legislation by Constitution Day.” Last month, hardliners including Democratic Party lawmakers Seo Young-kyo and Kim Yong-min, along with Rebuilding Korea Party lawmaker Park Eun-jung, proposed their own amendment to completely abolish prosecutors’ investigative and investigative command powers. The Ministry of Justice reportedly asked the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office for its opinion on this amendment. <<> Even within the Democratic Party, concerns are rising that “abolishing supplementary investigation powers without sufficient deliberation could lead to significant side effects.” Issues include potential investigative gaps in cases requiring urgent supplementary investigation, such as those with high risks of evidence tampering or imminent statutes of limitations, and the loss of checks on excessive police investigations. It is said that such criticisms have been echoed in recent Democratic Party lawmaker group chats. A first-term lawmaker from the Seoul metropolitan area with a legal background suggested, “Let’s conditionally recognize supplementary investigation powers only for cases where the police have filed an ‘opinion to indict’,” allowing for exceptions. Another second-term lawmaker from the same area reportedly posted, “We must consider whether victim protection will be sufficient and whether police power can be checked if supplementary investigation powers disappear.” Minister of Justice Jeong Seong-ho, who has consistently argued for the necessity of supplementary investigation powers, also told reporters that day, “Even if the government has its position, aren’t those over there [Democratic Party lawmakers] saying legislative power lies with the National Assembly? Won’t the excellent lawmakers discuss this well?” <<> President Lee Jae-myung had also maintained that it was necessary, but as a competition for distinctiveness between pro-Lee and pro-Cheong factions heated up ahead of the Democratic Party leadership election, he recently sided with the hardliners, stating “the National Assembly will also bear responsibility for the side effects.” Former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, a candidate for party leadership, had also firmly stated in his final press conference as prime minister, “The government’s position is to abolish supplementary investigation powers.” <<> While the Democratic Party leadership is negative about the hardliners’ legislative speed push, it is reported that they may propose a revision to the Criminal Procedure Act led by the floor leadership as early as next week. A Democratic Party official said, “We intend to discuss the Criminal Procedure Act in the legislation and judiciary committee as soon as possible.” However, a key floor leadership figure noted, “There are many issues to consider, so it won’t be easy to pass the bill before the August 17 national convention.” <<> Alternatives under consideration include substantiating the prosecutor’s right to request supplementary investigations and making the police investigation review committee permanent to check police investigations. Another option being discussed is allowing prosecutors to request a change in the investigation team if the police do not comply with a legitimate supplementary investigation request. Democratic Party legislation and judiciary committee members are also debating whether to allow complainants the right to object in cases where the police decide not to forward the case for prosecution. Earlier in February, when conflict between the party and the government arose over this issue, the Democratic Party held a general meeting of lawmakers and decided party policy to abolish supplementary investigation powers but retain the right to request supplementary investigations. <<> The People Power Party criticized the move as “butchering the judicial system.” Floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik said, “The Democratic Party-controlled legislation and judiciary committee has become a ‘death judiciary’ (playing on the word ‘beop’ for law and ‘sa’ for death), where the rule of law has died. These lawmakers, intoxicated by the cheers of hardline supporters, will slash the rule of law with the blade of power.” He added, “If we completely separate investigation and prosecution and even eliminate supplementary investigation powers, the endless ping-pong of cases between investigative agencies will only increase. This will ultimately be passed on as the victim’s suffering.” (한병도 민주당 당대표 직무대행 겸 원내대표는 3일 당 회의에서 “검찰 개혁의 화룡점정이 될 형사소송법 개정은 원내, 정책위원회, 법제사법위원회가 힘을 합쳐 내용은 충실하게, 처리는 쾌속으로 진행하겠다”고 말했다. 형사소송법 개정안에는 검찰의 보완수사권을 전면 폐지하는 내용이 담길 예정이다. 이와 관련, 민주당은 전날 형사소송법 개정 TF를 꾸리고 본격적인 법 개정 절차에 돌입했다. 이를 위해 국민의힘이 민주당의 일방적인 상임위원장 선출 강행에 반발하며 국회 일정을 전면 보이콧하고 있는 상황에서도 민주당은 전날 야당 없이 22대 국회 후반기 첫 법사위를 열었다.)

item.title: Party Leadership Hopefuls Gather: Smiles Inside, Friction Outside (與 당권 주자 한자리에… 만나선 웃음꽃, 나가선 신경전)
item.description:
Party Leadership Hopefuls Gather: Smiles Inside, Friction Outside (與 당권 주자 한자리에… 만나선 웃음꽃, 나가선 신경전)

Ahead of the August 17 Democratic Party of Korea convention, party leadership candidates—former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, Lawmaker Song Young-gil, and former Party Leader Chung Cheong-rae—met together on the 3rd at a parliamentary workshop. On-site, a friendly atmosphere prevailed, but before the event, Kim and Song had clashed with Chung, criticizing his hardline stance. (더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회를 앞두고 당권 주자인 김민석 전 국무총리와 송영길 의원, 정청래 전 대표가 3일 당 국회의원 워크숍에서 한자리에 모였다. 현장에선 화기애애한 분위기가 연출됐지만 이날 행사 전까지 김 전 총리와 송 의원은 정 전 대표의 강경 노선 등을 비판하며 대립각을 세웠다.)

At the head table in a hotel in Yongsan District, Seoul, Kim, Song, and Chung sat side by side. The three exchanged light conversation with smiles. Prime Minister Han Sung-sook, Acting Democratic Party Leader Han Byung-do, and Presidential Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik also sat at the same table. Before taking their seats, Kim and Chung circulated among the tables, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries with lawmakers. Song, who arrived first, briefly greeted a few lawmakers, gave a media interview, and quickly headed to his seat. A Democratic Party official observing the scene noted, “Kim and Chung repeatedly laughed loudly, but even before their official candidacy announcements, they were effectively campaigning, with their respective supporters following closely behind.” <<> The leadership hopefuls continued their subtle rivalry outside the venue. Notably, Kim and Song, backed by the pro-Myeong faction, attacked Chung over local election results, the one-member-one-vote system for delegates and party members, and prosecutorial reform. (이날 서울 용산구의 한 호텔에 마련된 행사장 헤드테이블에는 김 전 총리와 송 의원, 정 전 대표가 나란히 앉았다. 세 사람은 웃으면서 가볍게 대화를 주고받았다. 한성숙 국무총리, 한병도 민주당 대표 직무대행, 강훈식 대통령비서실장 등도 같은 테이블에 앉았다. 자리에 앉기 전 김 전 총리와 정 전 대표는 각 테이블을 돌며 의원들과 악수하고 덕담을 나눴다. 가장 먼저 도착한 송 의원은 몇몇 의원과 간단히 인사를 나눈 뒤 언론 인터뷰를 하고 곧장 자리로 향했다. 이를 지켜본 민주당 관계자는 “김 전 총리와 정 전 대표가 연신 크게 웃었지만, 공식 출마 선언 전부터 선거운동을 하고 각자 지지하는 의원들이 그 뒤를 따르는 모습이었다”고 말했다.)

In a radio interview, Kim remarked, “People often jokingly call (the Democratic Party) the ‘ruling party in opposition,’ but is that acceptable? The party needs major innovation.” This was interpreted as a critique that the ruling party, led by Chung over the past year, had focused on hardline struggles rather than supporting the government. Regarding Chung and Song, Kim added, “Both have already served as party leader, while I haven’t. The party’s key task now is the general election in two years, and I’m the only one who has directly overseen and led general elections, presidential elections, and local elections to victory.” Song criticized pro-Chung North Jeolla Province Governor Lee Won-taek for raising a “North Jeolla neglect” narrative related to the president’s three major mega-projects, calling it “inappropriate remarks” and noting that “Chung somewhat echoed that sentiment.” (당권 주자들은 이날 행사장 밖에서 신경전을 이어갔다. 특히 친명계가 지지하는 김 전 총리와 송 의원은 지방선거 결과와 대의원·권리당원 1인 1표제, 검찰 개편 등을 두고 정 전 대표를 공격했다.)

In response, Chung said, “That came from merchants and residents, not from me. My intention was to address their sense of loss—how could I encourage that? You shouldn’t twist the meaning of someone’s words.” On the pro-Myeong faction’s calls to amend the one-member-one-vote system he championed, he asserted, “This is an attempt to undermine the one-member-one-vote system, and not a single inch of it should be altered.” It was reported that after the workshop, a lawmaker posted in a group Telegram chat a swipe at Chung, writing, “He’s been avoiding eye contact since some criticism. Still, you’ve got to shake hands. Let’s not be petty.” (김 전 총리는 라디오 인터뷰에서 “(민주당을) ‘집권 야당’이라고 흔히 농처럼 이야기하는데, 그래서 되겠는가”라며 “당이 대대적인 혁신을 해야 한다”고 했다. 지난 1년간 정 전 대표가 이끈 여당이 정부를 뒷받침하기보다는 강경파 중심의 투쟁을 했다는 뜻으로 해석됐다. 정 전 대표와 송 의원을 향해선 “두 분은 당대표를 이미 해보셨고, 저는 아직 안 해봤지 않나”라며 “지금 당의 중요한 과제는 2년 후 총선인데, 제가 총선, 대선, 지방선거를 다 직접 총괄·지휘해보고 승리까지 이끌어본 유일한 사람”이라고도 했다. 송 의원은 친청계 이원택 전북지사가 대통령이 이끄는 3대 메가 프로젝트와 관련해 ‘전북 소외론’을 꺼내 든 것에 대해 “적절치 않은 발언”이라며 “정 전 대표도 거기에 약간 동조하는 말씀을 했다”고 했다.)

At the workshop, the Democratic Party discussed strategies for the latter half of the 22nd National Assembly and declared it would ramp up legislative efforts to push forward the second-year agenda of the Lee Jae-myung administration. Acting Leader Han Byung-do stated, “We will unite the party, government, and presidential office to reaffirm the ruling party’s responsibilities and complete livelihood legislation without a hitch. We aim to finalize key national policy legislation by year’s end.” Criticizing the People Power Party, Han added that the party would revise the filibuster and fast-track systems—tools of minority opposition resistance—to speed up legislation. However, no mention was made of cooperation with the opposition. (이에 대해 정 전 대표는 “상인, 도민들이 한 것이지 제가 그 말을 한 것은 아니다”라며 “상실감을 만회할 수 있도록 하겠다는 뜻이지 어떻게 제가 그걸 부추기겠나. 사람 말의 진의를 비틀면 안 된다”고 했다. 자신이 주도한 1인 1표제를 두고 친명계가 보완책을 요구하는 것에 대해선 “1인 1표제를 흔들려는 것인데, 일점일획이라도 흔들려선 안 된다”고 했다. 이날 워크숍 후 단체 텔레그램방에는 한 의원이 정 전 대표를 저격하며 “이런 저런 비판을 했다고 시선을 피하던데. 그래도 악수는 해야죠. 이러진 맙시다. 쪼잔하게”라는 글을 올리기도 했다고 한다.)

In a lecture on the second-year governance direction and plans, Presidential Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik urged, “The public changes very rapidly, and politics is a 100% demand-driven market. I hope the Democratic Party becomes a party that responds well to public demands.” Regarding the party’s low approval ratings among the 2030 generation, he said, “We need to secure over 50% support from the youth.” Kang also pointed to the overheating of the Seoul metropolitan area due to recent semiconductor industry growth and called for active efforts toward balanced regional development. (민주당은 이날 워크숍에서 22대 후반기 국회 운영 전략을 논의하고 이재명 정부 2년 차 국정 과제 추진을 위한 입법 드라이브를 걸겠다고 선언했다. 한병도 대행은 “당·정·청이 하나 돼서 집권 여당의 책임을 되새기고 차질 없이 민생 입법을 완수하겠다”며 “주요 국정과제 입법을 올해 연말까지 마무리하겠다”고 했다. 국민의힘을 비판하며 소수 야당의 저항 수단인 필리버스터(무제한 토론)와 패스트트랙(신속 처리 안건) 제도를 고쳐 입법에 속도를 내겠다고도 했다. 다만 야당과의 협치 등에 대해선 언급이 없었다.)

item.title: [Behind the Scenes in Yeouido] Jang, Han, and Lee: An Unexpected First Three-Way Meeting at a Funeral Home ([여의도 비하인드] 장·한·석, 장례식장서 뜻밖의 첫 삼자대면)
item.description:
[Behind the Scenes in Yeouido] Jang, Han, and Lee: An Unexpected First Three-Way Meeting at a Funeral Home ([여의도 비하인드] 장·한·석, 장례식장서 뜻밖의 첫 삼자대면)

At around 10 p.m. on the 2nd, at a university hospital funeral home in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province. Lee Jun-seok, leader of the Reform Party, and independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon visited the bereaved family of People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyuk. This marked the first time the three, often described as “rivals” within the conservative camp, sat together in the same room. <<> According to attendees, Representative Lee arrived first, paid his respects, and sat at a four-person table. Han arrived shortly after and took a seat across from Lee. Representative Jang sat next to Han. Despite the late hour, about 30 mourners were present at the time. <<> Han offered words of condolence to Jang, who responded with a sentiment akin to “Thank you for coming.” Jang reportedly emptied a glass of soju poured by Han without a word. The conversation then continued intermittently for about 20 minutes, led by Representative Lee. A political figure at the scene said, “It was more about sharing Jang’s grief than discussing current political issues.” <<> Jang currently serves as the leader of the People Power Party, while Lee and Han have both previously held the same position but were ousted by the party’s pro-Yoon faction. The three have politically clashed, often checking each other. <<> Earlier, Jang expelled Han over the “party member bulletin board” issue. Han has expressed a desire to rejoin the People Power Party while demanding Jang’s resignation. Lee, who leads the Reform Party, has criticized both Jang’s and Han’s actions. <<> Given this context, it was rare for the three to sit together. Jang and Han had not sat down for a conversation since the impeachment crisis of former President Yoon in December 2024. It was also the first time Lee and Han sat together. Jang and Lee were known to have had no exchanges since a lunch meeting in late March, about two months before the local elections. <<> The meeting ended when Han stood up to head to his district in Busan. A political figure noted, “Since it was a condolence visit, it’s hard to assign political meaning to this meeting,” but added, “Many mourners were talking about how the relationship among the three might evolve.” <<> Meanwhile, it was reported that President Lee Jae-myung also sent a condolence wreath to Jang’s family funeral. A presidential office official said, “Although relations between the ruling and opposition parties are strained, the president believes it’s proper to show respect to the leader of the main opposition party.” (지난 2일 밤 10시 경기 수원시의 한 대학병원 장례식장. 국민의힘 장동혁 대표 가족 상가(喪家)에 이준석 개혁신당 대표, 무소속 한동훈 의원이 조문했다. 보수 진영 내 ‘앙숙’으로 평가받는 세 사람이 한자리에 마주 앉은 것은 이번이 처음이다.)

item.title: Lee’s Approval Rating Rises to 54%, Rebounding After Three Weeks (李 지지율 54%… 3주 만에 반등)
item.description:
Lee’s Approval Rating Rises to 54%, Rebounding After Three Weeks (李 지지율 54%… 3주 만에 반등)

A survey released on the 3rd showed a rebound in President Lee Jae-myung’s approval rating, which had been on a downward trend recently. In a poll conducted by Gallup Korea from the 30th of last month to the 2nd of this month among 1,005 adults aged 18 and over nationwide, 54% of respondents said President Lee is “doing well” in his job performance. This marks a 3 percentage point increase in positive evaluations compared to last week’s survey. Negative evaluations dropped by 5 percentage points to 36%. (최근 하락세를 보이던 이재명 대통령의 국정 지지율이 반등한 조사 결과가 3일 나왔다. 한국갤럽이 지난달 30일부터 지난 2일까지 전국 만 18세 이상 1005명을 대상으로 한 조사에서 이 대통령의 직무 수행에 “잘하고 있다”는 응답은 전체의 54%였다. 지난주 조사보다 긍정 평가가 3%p(포인트) 오른 것이다. 부정 평가는 5%p 하락한 36%였다.)

President Lee’s approval rating had fallen to 57% in a survey on the 12th of last month, a 7-percentage-point drop from the previous week, marking its first dip into the 50% range since February. In a survey released on the 26th of the same month, it further declined to 51%, putting the 50% threshold at risk, but it has now rebounded. Gallup analyzed that this was influenced by President Lee’s announcement at the presidential office on the 29th of last month of the "Three Major Mega Projects," worth 1,500 trillion won, including the "Honam Semiconductor" initiative. (이 대통령의 국정 지지율은 지난달 12일 조사에서 57%로 전주보다 7%p 하락하며 2월 이후 처음 50%대로 내려왔다. 같은 달 26일 발표된 조사에서는 51%까지 하락하며 50% 선이 위협받았는데, 이날 반등한 것이다. 갤럽은 이 대통령이 지난달 29일 청와대에서 발표한 ‘호남 반도체’ 등 1500조원 규모의 ‘3대 메가 프로젝트’ 발표 등의 영향이 있었다고 분석했다.)

However, evaluations of the Lee administration’s real estate policy showed that 46% of respondents felt it was “doing poorly,” which was 20 percentage points higher than the 26% who said it was “doing well.” Notably, negative evaluations exceeded half among the 2030 generation. In their 20s, negative evaluations stood at 51%, while among those in their 30s, it was 56%, the highest across all age groups. (그러나 이재명 정부의 부동산 정책에 대한 평가는 “잘못하고 있다”는 응답이 46%로, “잘하고 있다”는 응답 26%보다 20%p가 높았다. 특히 2030 세대에서 부정 평가가 절반을 넘었다. 20대에서 부정 평가는 51%였고, 30대의 부정 평가는 56%로 전 연령대에서 가장 높았다.)

Meanwhile, President Lee will attend the NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) summit in Ankara, Turkey, on the 7th and 8th. This marks his first attendance at a NATO summit since taking office. Following this, President Lee will visit Mongolia from the 9th to the 11th. This is the first state visit by a South Korean president in 15 years. (한편 이재명 대통령이 7~8일 튀르키예 앙카라에서 열리는 나토(NATO·북대서양조약기구) 정상회의에 참석한다. 취임 후 나토 정상회의에 참석하는 것은 이번이 처음이다. 이후 이 대통령은 9~11일 몽골을 방문한다. 한국 대통령으로서는 15년 만에 이뤄진 국빈 방문이다.)

Cheong Wa Dae National Security Office Director Wi Sung-lac stated in a briefing at the presidential office on the 3rd, “President Lee will attend the NATO summit at the invitation of NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, and then visit Mongolia at the invitation of Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh.” President Lee skipped last year’s NATO summit in the Netherlands, held just after his inauguration, citing worsening conditions in the Middle East. (위성락 청와대 국가안보실장은 3일 청와대에서 브리핑을 통해 “이 대통령이 마크 뤼터 나토 사무총장의 초청으로 나토 정상회의에 참석한 뒤, 오흐나 후렐수흐 몽골 대통령의 초청으로 몽골을 방문한다”고 밝혔다. 이 대통령은 취임 직후였던 지난해 6월 네덜란드에서 열린 나토 정상회의에 중동 정세 악화 등을 이유로 불참했다.)

At that time, Director Wi attended in his stead, which led to speculation from the opposition that “he may have skipped it due to concerns about China and Russia.” NATO, a security alliance of the U.S. and Europe, has been at odds with Russia and China. Regarding the possibility of adopting a joint statement on China and Russia during this NATO visit, Director Wi said, “There are no joint documents related to us.” On the strained relations between the U.S. and NATO-affiliated European countries, he added, “The U.S. does not differ from us in its overall thinking on cooperation with NATO.” (당시 위 실장이 대신 참석했는데, 이를 두고 야권에선 “중국과 러시아를 의식해 불참한 것 아니냐”는 말이 나왔다. 미국과 유럽의 안보 동맹인 나토는 러시아·중국과 대립해 왔다. 위 실장은 이번 나토 순방 중 대중국·대러시아 공동 성명 채택 가능성과 관련해 “우리와 관련된 공동 문건은 없다”고 했다. 미국과 나토 소속 유럽 국가들의 관계가 좋지 않은 데 대해서는 “미국 역시 나토와의 협력 전반에 대해서는 우리와 생각이 다른 것이 없다”고 했다.)

item.title: Lee Byung-tae: "Even Shouting 'Long Live Kim Il-sung' in the Heart of Seoul Should Be Allowed" (이병태 “서울 한복판에서 ‘김일성 만세’ 외쳐도 허용돼야”)
item.description:
Lee Byung-tae: "Even Shouting 'Long Live Kim Il-sung' in the Heart of Seoul Should Be Allowed" (이병태 “서울 한복판에서 ‘김일성 만세’ 외쳐도 허용돼야”)

Lee Byung-tae, vice chairman of the Presidential Regulatory Reform Committee, said on the 4th regarding Baejae High School's baseball team receiving heavy disciplinary action over the 'Starbucks cheer chant' controversy, "Even shouting 'Long Live Kim Il-sung' in the heart of Seoul should be allowed." Regarding calls for his resignation from some within the ruling bloc, he dismissed them, saying, "Criticism is also freedom of expression." (이병태 대통령 직속 규제합리화위원회 부위원장은 4일 배재고 야구부가 ‘스타벅스 응원 구호’ 논란으로 중징계를 받은 것에 대해 “서울 한복판에서 ‘김일성 만세’를 외쳐도 허용돼야 한다”고 했다. 여권 일각에서 나오는 사퇴 요구에 대해선 “비판도 표현의 자유”라며 일축했다.)

On the 4th, Vice Chairman Lee posted an article titled "Freedom of Expression and Baseball Cheer Chants" on his Facebook page, stating, "Freedom of expression is a fundamental right to speak thoughts that the majority disagrees with, without fear of punishment," and thus expressed this view. (이 부위원장은 4일 자신의 페이스북에 ‘표현의 자유 그리고 야구 응원 구호’라는 제목의 글을 올려 “표현의 자유는 다수가 동의하지 않는 생각을 처벌의 두려움 없이 말할 수 있는 기본권”이라며 이같이 밝혔다.)

Vice Chairman Lee said, "The core of freedom of expression is not censorship but belief in the 'self-purifying power of truth.' It is not the right to say what is right and correct, but a fundamental right for society to allow even wrong, absurd, and false statements." He added, "The crazy words of a minority are purified by the truth of the majority." (이 부위원장은 “표현의 자유의 핵심은 검열이 아니라 ‘진리의 자정 능력’을 믿는 것”이라며 “옳고 바른 말을 할 권리가 아니라, 틀리고 엉뚱하고 거짓된 말도 사회가 허용하라는 기본권”이라고 했다. 그는 “소수의 미친 소리는 다수의 진리에 의해 정화된다”고 했다.)

Regarding the calls from some within the ruling bloc for his resignation over his claim that Baejae High School's discipline was "like North Korea," he directly rebutted. Vice Chairman Lee said, "Whether the cheer chant was appropriate may vary from person to person," but added, "If it was inappropriate, one can criticize it. That criticism itself is freedom of expression, but punishing someone based on their speech is a denial of fundamental rights." (배재고 징계를 “북한과 같다”고 했던 자신의 주장을 두고 범여권 일각에서 사퇴 요구가 나오는 데 대해서도 정면 반박했다. 이 부위원장은 “응원 구호가 적절했는지는 사람마다 다를 것”이라면서도 “부적절했다면 비판하면 된다. 그 비판도 표현의 자유지만, 발언을 근거로 처벌하는 것은 기본권의 부인”이라고 했다.)

He continued, "Denying that this speech should be punished is a denial of the democracy pursued by the Gwangju Democratization Movement," adding, "A society where fundamental rights are not protected is not a democratic society. The desire for severe punishment starts from the sanctification of ideas." (이어 “이 발언이 처벌받아야 한다는 기본권의 부정은 광주 민주화운동이 추구했던 민주주의를 부정하는 것”이라며 “기본권이 지켜지지 않는 사회는 민주적 사회가 아니다. 엄벌의 욕구는 사상의 성역화에서 출발한다”고 했다.)

Vice Chairman Lee said, "I still firmly believe that the participants and victims of the Gwangju Democratization Movement fought for democracy in this land," and "If you agree with this, you must not deny the universally recognized fundamental right of democracy: freedom of expression." He added, "Protecting fundamental rights is how we complete the Gwangju Democratization Movement," and "That is why I believe it is not the students' chant but their punishment that mocks and belittles the Gwangju Democratization Movement." <<>> (이 부위원장은 “나는 광주 민주화 운동의 참여자나 희생자가 이 땅의 민주주의를 위해 싸웠다고 지금도 굳게 믿고 있다”며 “이것에 동의한다면 민주주의의 인류 보편적 기본권인 표현의 자유를 부인해서는 안 된다”고 했다. 그러면서 “기본권을 지키는 것이 광주 민주화운동을 완성하는 일”이라며 “그래서 나는 학생들의 구호가 아니라 그들의 처벌이 광주민주화운동의 조롱과 폄훼라고 믿는다”고 했다.)

item.title: Lee Byung-tae: "Is the May 18 a Sanctuary?" Choi Min-hee: "Yes, It Is." (이병태 “5·18 성역인가" 최민희 “네, 성역 맞습니다”)
item.description:
Lee Byung-tae: "Is the May 18 a Sanctuary?" Choi Min-hee: "Yes, It Is." (이병태 “5·18 성역인가" 최민희 “네, 성역 맞습니다”)

As political controversy spreads surrounding Baejae High School's baseball team, which received severe punishment for a 'Starbucks cheering song', Choi Min-hee, a member of the Democratic Party of Korea, stated, "The May 18 Democratic Uprising is indeed a sanctuary of democracy." <<> On the 3rd, Rep. Choi posted on her Facebook and X (formerly Twitter): "Deputy Chairman Lee Byung-tae of the Regulatory Reform Committee asks, 'Is the May 18 a sanctuary?' Here is my answer: 'Yes, it is. It is a sanctuary of democracy.'" <<> This is a public rebuttal of Lee Byung-tae, deputy chairman of the Presidential Regulatory Reform Committee, who had previously said regarding the severe punishment of Baejae High School's baseball team for mocking the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement: "The May 18 has become a sanctuary" and "It looks like something from North Korea." <<> In response to Deputy Chairman Lee's remarks, criticism is mounting among pro-Moon and pro-Cheong supporters within the conservative camp. On the 'Ddanji Ilbo' message board and social media, popular among pro-Moon and pro-Cheong followers, critical posts are appearing such as: "Why put such a person in a presidential agency?" "New Lee Jae-myung, you'll fail like this," and "The true nature of the New Lee Jae-myung is revealed." <<> Deputy Chairman Lee Byung-tae, a former KAIST professor and close associate of former Daegu Mayor Hong Joon-pyo, is referred to as a 'New Lee Jae-myung' figure appointed by President Lee. During the last presidential election, President Lee attempted to bring Deputy Chairman Lee into his campaign committee, but his past 'inflammatory remarks' against former President Moon Jae-in were criticized, and the plan was abandoned due to opposition from some figures. <<> Even after President Lee announced Deputy Chairman Lee's appointment on the 3rd, the Fatherland Innovation Party and Democratic Party lawmaker Park Joo-min have been demanding, "Please reconsider the selection." (‘스타벅스 응원가’로 중징계를 받은 배재고 야구부를 둘러싼 정치권 논란이 확산하는 가운데, 최민희 더불어민주당 의원이 “5·18은 민주주의의 성역이 맞다”고 밝혔다.)

item.title: Blue House Warns Lee Byung-tae: "Inappropriate Conduct for Someone in a Responsible Position" (靑, 이병태에 “책임있는 위치의 사람으로서 부적절한 처신”)
item.description:
Blue House Warns Lee Byung-tae: "Inappropriate Conduct for Someone in a Responsible Position" (靑, 이병태에 “책임있는 위치의 사람으로서 부적절한 처신” )

The presidential office Cheong Wa Dae issued a stern warning on the 4th regarding Lee Byung-tae, Vice Chairman of the Presidential Committee on Regulatory Reform, for criticizing the disciplinary action against Baejae High School's baseball team, stating that "as someone in a responsible position within a government-affiliated agency, his conduct was inappropriate." (청와대가 4일 이병태 대통령 직속 규제합리화위원회 부위원장이 배재고 야구부 징계 사태를 비판한 것에 대해 “정부 소속 기관의 책임있는 위치의 사람으로서 부적절한 처신”이라며 엄중 경고했다고 밝혔다.)

Kang Yoo-jung, Senior Presidential Secretary for Public Relations, stated that day, "Vice Chairman Lee Byung-tae posted personal opinions on social media," adding, "This carries the risk of misunderstanding, contrary to the government's firm stance against hatred and ridicule." (강유정 청와대 수석대변인은 이날 “이병태 규제합리화위원회 부위원장이 개인적 의견을 SNS에 게시한 바 있다”며 “이는 혐오와 조롱에 대한 정부의 단호한 거부 기조와 달리 오해의 소지가 있다”고 했다.)

Earlier, on the 2nd, Vice Chairman Lee posted on his social media that the Baejae High School baseball team, which had chanted a "Starbucks cheer song" directed at Gwangju Jeil High School during a game and faced heavy disciplinary action amid controversy over disparaging the May 18 Democratic Uprising, was "like North Korea" and that "May 18 has become a sacred cow." As criticism from within the ruling bloc emerged, he continued his argument on the 4th, saying, "This denies the democracy (freedom of expression) that the Gwangju Democratization Movement pursued." (앞서 이 부위원장은 지난 2일 자신의 SNS를 통해 배재고 야구부가 경기 도중 광주제일고를 향해 ‘스타벅스 응원가’를 구호로 외쳐 5·18 폄훼 논란으로 중징계를 받자 “북한 같다” “5·18이 성역이 됐다”고 했다. 이를 두고 범여권 비판이 나오자, 4일에도 “광주 민주화운동이 추구했던 민주주의(표현의 자유)를 부정하는 것”이라며 주장을 이어갔다.)

In response, Senior Secretary Kang stated, "Especially as someone in a responsible position within a government-affiliated agency, this was inappropriate conduct," and "We have issued a stern warning and strongly requested that such incidents be prevented from recurring in the future." <<>> (이에 대해 강 수석대변인은 “특히 정부 소속 기관의 책임있는 위치의 사람으로서 부적절한 처신”이라며 “이에 엄중히 경고하고, 향후 재발 방지를 강력히 요청했음을 알린다”고 했다.)

item.title: Lee: "If mega projects were a tool for approval ratings, I would have launched them before the local elections." (李 “메가 프로젝트, 지지율 수단이었다면 지방선거 전에 했을 것”)
item.description:
Lee: "If mega projects were a tool for approval ratings, I would have launched them before the local elections." (李 “메가 프로젝트, 지지율 수단이었다면 지방선거 전에 했을 것”)

President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 4th, "If the three mega projects were a political tool for managing approval ratings, I would have started them before the local elections." (이재명 대통령은 4일 “3대 메가 프로젝트가 지지율 관리를 위한 정치적 수단이었다면 지방선거 전에 시작했을 것”이라고 했다.)

On X (formerly Twitter) that day, the President said, "It has long been my belief that approval ratings naturally follow from performance and results." This appears to be a response to political interpretations, such as claims from the political sphere that the government's announcement of a large-scale semiconductor cluster in the Honam region was "made with the Democratic Party's national convention in mind." (이 대통령은 이날 X(옛 트위터)에 “지지율은 성과와 실적을 자연스럽게 따라온다는 게 저의 오래된 생각”이라며 이같이 밝혔다. 정부가 호남에 대규모 반도체 클러스터 조성을 발표한 것을 두고 정치권에서 ‘민주당 전당대회를 염두한 것’이라는 등의 정치적 해석이 나오는 데 따른 반응으로 보인다.)

The President added, "The grand transformation of the national territory—comparable to a sea change for a world-changing upheaval—has been a dream of mine long before my inauguration," and "Right after taking office, I made national-level preparations for large-scale local investment and development aimed at balanced growth, seeking cooperation from the business community, but progress was slow." (이 대통령은 “천지개벽을 위한 상전벽해 수준의 국토대전환은 제가 취임하기 전 아주 오래전부터 꿈꿔왔던 일”이라며 “취임 직후부터 균형발전을 위한 대규모 지방투자와 개발을 위해 국가 차원의 준비를 하며 경제계에 협조 요청을 해 왔는데 속도가 크게 나지 않았다”고 했다.)

He continued, "Then, recently, as the government's focus on investment in future advanced industries like artificial intelligence aligned with a structural, long-term, and explosive positive restructuring of the AI semiconductor industry, large-scale local investment became possible." (이어 “그러던 중 최근에 정부의 인공지능 등 미래 첨단선업 중점 투자정책과 인공지능 반도체 산업의 구조적이고 장기적이며 폭발적인 긍정적 재편이 맞물리며 대규모 지방투자가 가능하게 되었다”고 했다.)

The President also shared media reports showing a rebound in his approval ratings following the announcement of the three mega projects. His approval rating had fallen to 51% in a Gallup Korea survey released on the 26th of last month, threatening the 50% threshold, but it rebounded to 54% in the same survey released the previous day. (이 대통령은 3대 메가프로젝트 발표 후 국정 지지율이 반등했다는 언론 보도도 공유했다. 이 대통령 국정 지지율은 지난달 26일 발표된 한국갤럽 조사에서 51%까지 하락하며 50% 선이 위협받았는데, 전날 발표된 같은 조사에선 54%로 반등했다.)

The President said, "Approval ratings are important, but more important are the performance and results that improve the lives of the people," adding, "Approval ratings are like the wind—coming and going, sometimes strong, sometimes weak. But results and achievements are like a mountain—they don't change easily." (이 대통령은 “지지율도 중요하지만 더 중요한건 국민의 삶을 개선할 성과와 실적”이라며 “지지율은 바람같은 것이어서 오기도 가기도 하고, 강하기도 약하기도 하지만 실적과 성과는 산 같은 것이어서 쉽게 변하지 않는다”고 했다.)
